name: Isolated Angioid Streaks

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnosis of isolated angioid streaks

criteria.description: Presence of irregular, radiating, crack-like dehiscences in Bruch's membrane visible on fundoscopic examination
No clinical or laboratory evidence of systemic diseases commonly associated with angioid streaks (e.g., pseudoxanthoma elasticum, Ehlers-Danlos syndrome)
Confirmation of angioid streaks by fluorescein angiography or optical coherence tomography
Assessment of visual acuity and presence of choroidal neovascularization

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic fundoscopic findings of angioid streaks confirmed by imaging, with exclusion of systemic diseases known to cause angioid streaks
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; systemic evaluation is essential to exclude associated disorders.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Radiating crack-like dehiscences of Bruch's membrane
pathognomonic.notes: Visible on fundoscopic examination as angioid streaks

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic fundus pigmentation changes adjacent to streaks

common.symptomName: Decreased visual acuity due to choroidal neovascularization
searchTerms: blurred vision from new blood vessels
vision loss due to eye vessel growth
reduced sight from abnormal eye vessels

occasional.symptomName: Retinal pigment epithelium atrophy adjacent to streaks
searchTerms: eye pigment layer thinning near streaks
damage to retinal pigment near streaks
loss of eye pigment cells adjacent to streaks

rare.symptomName: Secondary glaucoma due to neovascular complications
searchTerms: increased eye pressure due to vessel growth

laboratory: Exclusion of systemic diseases by negative genetic and biochemical testing for pseudoxanthoma elasticum, Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, sickle cell disease
imaging: Optical coherence tomography revealing breaks in Bruch's membrane
genetic: No pathogenic variants associated with systemic connective tissue disorders detected
other: Visual acuity testing showing decreased vision if choroidal neovascularization present

distinguishingFeatures: Positive genetic testing for ABCC6 mutations
Presence of sickled erythrocytes on blood smear

redFlags: Signs of choroidal neovascular membrane formation
Presence of systemic symptoms suggestive of connective tissue disorder
references: Gass JD. Stereoscopic Atlas of Macular Diseases. 4th ed. 1997.
Khan KN, et al. Angioid streaks: clinical features and systemic associations. Eye (Lond). 2019.
